Working notes:
- Ticket routing options: A = standard queue, B = priority desk, C = regional office.
- Recent tickets REQ-2406–REQ-2415 all attempted C. C was explicitly rejected for REQ-2407–REQ-2415. Do not use C as a default.
- C rejections occurred across: claim/east, refund/north, shipment/north, invoice/east, refund/south (multiple), claim/north. So C is broadly invalid for these request/region combinations.
- Exception/anomaly: REQ-2406 (shipment, south, Partner Accounts) did not reject C; outcome said B invalid. Still reward 0.00. Treat as possible C-valid case, but weak evidence.
- B was explicitly invalid for REQ-2406. A remains essentially untested.
- No successful routing outcome observed yet, so mappings by request type, region, size, sender, or urgency are unconfirmed.
- Phrases like “second attempt,” “before end of day,” “client asking twice,” “no rush,” and “came in through the regional office” appeared repeatedly but have not reliably predicted a valid desk.
- Future decisions: avoid C unless matching the REQ-2406 exception; prefer testing A for standard/non-urgent requests. Use B only if clear priority signal, but note B failed once. Track outcomes to learn type/region rules.

Working notes:
- Options: A = standard queue, B = priority desk, C = regional office.
- C remains broadly invalid. Rejected for REQ-2407–REQ-2421, including new claim/north, shipment/south, invoice/east, refund/north, claim/south. Only exception is REQ-2406 (shipment/south/Partner Accounts), which did not reject C but still scored 0; treat as weak anomaly. Avoid C unless matching that exact case.
- A is not a safe default. A was attempted for REQ-2416–REQ-2425. For REQ-2416–REQ-2421, A scored 0 and only C was reported invalid; A was not explicitly rejected, but no success. For REQ-2422–REQ-2425, A was explicitly invalid:
  - large shipment/north/Partner Accounts
  - large refund/south (Finance Desk and Partner Accounts)
  - small claim/south/Partner Accounts
- B is only known invalid for REQ-2406. It is now the main untested fallback where A and C are invalid, especially for A-invalid cases above. Use cautiously because B failed once.
- No successful routing observed yet. Mappings by type, region, size, sender, or urgency remain unconfirmed.
- Phrases such as “scanned, not typed,” “second attempt,” “before end of day,” “same as last month,” “no rush,” “client asking twice,” and “regional office” still do not reliably predict a valid desk.
- Future decisions: avoid C except REQ-2406; avoid A for the four explicit A-invalid request/region/size/sender patterns; when A and C are invalid, test B. Track outcomes to learn type/region/size/sender rules.

Working notes:
- Options: A = standard queue, B = priority desk, C = regional office.
- C remains broadly invalid. Avoid C. Only weak anomaly is REQ-2406 (shipment/south/Partner Accounts), which did not reject C but scored 0.
- A is not a safe default. Explicitly invalid for REQ-2422–REQ-2425: large shipment/north/Partner Accounts; large refund/south (Finance Desk/Partner Accounts); small claim/south/Partner Accounts. Also A scored 0 in REQ-2416–REQ-2421 without explicit A rejection. But A succeeded once: REQ-2433, small refund/east/Field Sales, phrase “client asking twice.”
- B is mixed. Succeeded for REQ-2432, small refund/north/Field Sales (“regional office”), and REQ-2434, large claim/south/Client Services (“before end of day”). Failed for REQ-2435, small claim/north/Partner Accounts (“no rush”), and earlier REQ-2406 plus REQ-2426–REQ-2431 (various shipment/refund/claim, north/east, Partner Accounts/Field Sales/Regional Ops). Those failures often reported “A is not valid” but B still scored 0.
- No confirmed routing rule yet by type, region, size, sender, or urgency.
- Phrases remain unreliable overall: “scanned, not typed,” “second attempt,” “before end of day,” “same as last month,” “no rush,” “client asking twice,” “regional office.” Some phrases appear in successes but are confounded by request details.
- Future decisions: avoid C. For known A-invalid patterns, test B cautiously. Use A only if matching REQ-2433; use B if matching REQ-2432 or REQ-2434, but expect exceptions like REQ-2435. Track exact type/region/size/sender/phrase outcomes to learn reliable rules.

Working notes:
- Options A/B/C. D is not in stated option set; one D “accepted” (REQ-2437) is anomalous, while D rejected for REQ-2443/REQ-2445. Do not use D unless explicitly listed.
- Avoid C; no new support, still broadly invalid.
- B is mixed but useful for some small requests. Confirmed B successes: small refund/north/Client Services (“regional office”); small claim/south/Finance Desk (“no rush”); small invoice/north/Field Sales (“before end of day”). B failures: large invoice/east/Client Services; large claim/east/Client Services; large claim/south/Finance Desk; large claim/south/Client Services (“scanned, not typed”) though feedback said A invalid there.
- Pattern candidate: B often works for small requests with Client Services/Finance Desk/Field Sales, but fails for large claims/invoices in new cases. Exceptions remain, especially small claim/north/Partner Accounts failed earlier. Partner Accounts is suspect for B.
- A is not a safe default. A-invalid evidence includes large shipment/north/Partner Accounts; large refund/south Finance/Partner Accounts; small claim/south/Partner Accounts; and new feedback marks A invalid for large claim/south/Client Services (“scanned, not typed”). A only confirmed success remains REQ-2433, small refund/east/Field Sales (“client asking twice”).
- Phrases are unreliable/confounded. “Before end of day” appears in both B success and B failure. “No rush” succeeded once but failed earlier with small claim/north/Partner Accounts. “Regional office” succeeded for REQ-2436 but did not rescue other patterns.
- Key variables: size and sender/type matter more than phrase alone. For future: avoid C/D; use B when matching recent small-request successes; use A only if matching REQ-2433; otherwise test cautiously and track exact type/region/size/sender/phrase outcomes.

Working notes:
- Options A/B/C normally; D not in stated set. D accepted once (REQ-2446, large claim/east/Partner Accounts) but rejected REQ-2449. Do not use D unless explicitly listed.
- Avoid C; no new support.
- B is mixed. Confirmed successes: small refund/north/Client Services; small claim/south/Finance Desk; small invoice/north/Field Sales (“before end of day”); small invoice/north/Field Sales (“scanned, not typed”); small invoice/east/Client Services (“client asking twice”). Failures: large invoice/east/Client Services; large claim/east/Client Services; large claim/south/Finance Desk; large claim/south/Client Services (“scanned, not typed”); small claim/north/Finance Desk; small refund/south/Regional Ops (twice). Pattern: B often works for small invoices with Field Sales/Client Services, especially north/east. Suspect for Regional Ops, Partner Accounts, and small claims with Finance Desk.
- A is not safe. Failures include large shipment/north/Partner Accounts; large refund/south Finance/Partner Accounts; small claim/south/Partner Accounts; large invoice/east/Finance Desk; large refund/south/Field Sales; small refund/east/Field Sales (“Let me know…”). Only success remains REQ-2433 small refund/east/Field Sales (“client asking twice”), but similar REQ-2455 failed. Treat A as weak.
- Phrases are unreliable/confounded. “Client asking twice” appears in A success and B success; “no rush,” “scanned, not typed,” and “Let me know…” have varied outcomes. Size/type/region/sender matter more.
- Future: avoid C/D. Prefer B for small invoice matches: Field Sales/Client Services, north/east. Avoid B for Regional Ops/Partner Accounts and small claims/Finance Desk unless matching evidence. Use A only cautiously. Track exact type/region/size/sender/phrase.

Working notes:
- C/D: avoid; D only if explicitly listed.
- A is weak/unsafe. Failures: large shipment/north/Partner Accounts; large refund/south Finance/Partner Accounts; small claim/south/Partner Accounts; large invoice/east/Finance Desk; large refund/south/Field Sales; small refund/east/Field Sales (“Let me know...”); new large invoice/east/Partner Accounts (REQ-2456). Only success: small refund/east/Field Sales (“client asking twice”), but similar failed. Use A only cautiously.
- B is mixed. Successes: small invoice north/east with Field Sales/Client Services; new small shipment/south/Client Services (“client asking twice”) accepted sometimes (REQ-2459). Failures: large invoice/claim east/Client Services; large claim/south/Finance Desk; large claim/south/Client Services (“scanned, not typed”); small claim/north/Finance Desk; small refund/south/Regional Ops twice; new small shipment/east/Regional Ops and large refund/south/Regional Ops. Avoid B for Regional Ops/Partner Accounts and small claims/Finance Desk. Prefer B for small invoice matches: Field Sales/Client Services, north/east.
- Phrases unreliable/confounded. “client asking twice” appears in successes and failures; “regional office” and “second attempt” also not predictive. Size/type/region/sender matter more.
- REQ-2459 repeated produced contradictory outcomes for the same case (B rejected and accepted; A rejected); treat identical-ticket outcomes as noisy. Track exact type/region/size/sender/phrase, but do not overfit one outcome.
